newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel pledges quake relief to Iran despite row.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel pledges quake relief to Iran despite row.

text.p: Germany's Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said Bonn would not let a diplomatic row with Iran get in the way of helping the country's earthquake victims and pledged 500,000 marks in relief, his ministry said on Monday.

Kinkel said the sum would be given to the German Red Cross which planned to send a planeload of supplies to Iran on Tuesday for distribution in quake-sticken areas, a foreign ministry spokeswoman said.

"Diplomatic considerations should not be allowed to play a role here. We will allocate half a million marks at first," Kinkel told the Hamburger Morgenpost daily, referring to a diplomatic row sparked by a Berlin court's verdict that said Iran's leaders had ordered political killings in Germany.
"There is no question that we should try to help in such an emergency," he told the German daily.

Kinkel's relief pledge came as the world Red Cross body in Geneva appealed for $8.2 million for victims of Saturday's earthquake in Iran that killed about 2,400 people and left about 50,000 people homeless including some 6,000 injured.
The Red Cross in Germany said in a statement it would be sending out supplies that included tents, warm clothes and water bottles.
It also said that 4,300 volunteers working for the Red Crescent, its sister organisation in Islamic countries, would distribute the relief in Iran.
